title: OSHA construction silica practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction silica practice questions on 29 CFR 1926.1153. Every answer is explained and linked to the rule text.

questions.question: Under its scope paragraph, which occupational exposure to respirable crystalline silica in construction work is outside the coverage of 1926.1153?

options.A: Where the employer has fewer than ten employees
options.B: Where the work lasts less than one week
options.C: Where employee exposure will remain below 25 µg/m3 as an 8-hour TWA under any foreseeable conditions
options.D: Where the work is done outdoors

questions.explanation: The section applies to all occupational exposures in construction work "except where employee exposure will remain below 25 micrograms per cubic meter of air (25 µg/m3) as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA) under any foreseeable conditions."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 1926.1153 define "employee exposure" to respirable crystalline silica?

options.A: The exposure measured inside the employee's respirator
options.B: The exposure that would occur if the employee were not using a respirator
options.C: The average exposure of all employees on the site
options.D: The exposure measured at the edge of the work area

questions.explanation: Employee exposure means "the exposure to airborne respirable crystalline silica that would occur if the employee were not using a respirator."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the 1926.1153 definition, what must a competent person be capable of and authorized to do?

options.A: Identify existing and foreseeable silica hazards and take prompt corrective measures to eliminate or minimize them
options.B: Analyze air samples in an accredited laboratory
options.C: Sign medical opinions and order chest X-rays
options.D: Issue OSHA citations to other employers on the site

questions.explanation: A competent person is "capable of identifying existing and foreseeable respirable crystalline silica hazards in the workplace" and "has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate or minimize them."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the 1926.1153 definitions, who counts as a "specialist"?

options.A: Any NIOSH-certified B Reader
options.B: Any licensed respiratory therapist
options.C: The employer's competent person
options.D: An American Board Certified Specialist in Pulmonary Disease or in Occupational Medicine

questions.explanation: "Specialist means an American Board Certified Specialist in Pulmonary Disease or an American Board Certified Specialist in Occupational Medicine."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an employee doing a task listed on Table 1, what must the employer do unless it assesses and limits the employee's exposure under paragraph (d)?

options.A: Provide a respirator only if the employee asks for one
options.B: Fully and properly implement the engineering controls, work practices and respiratory protection specified for the task on Table 1
options.C: Do air monitoring every three months
options.D: Get written permission from OSHA before starting the task

questions.explanation: The employer "shall fully and properly implement the engineering controls, work practices, and respiratory protection specified for the task on Table 1, unless the employer assesses and limits the exposure of the employee" under paragraph (d).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee performs more than one Table 1 task in a shift, and all tasks combined last more than four hours. Which respiratory protection applies to each task?

options.A: The protection for the single longest task only
options.B: The protection specified for less than four hours per shift
options.C: No respirator, because each task alone is under four hours
options.D: The protection specified for more than four hours per shift

questions.explanation: Where the total duration of all Table 1 tasks combined "is more than four hours, the required respiratory protection for each task is the respiratory protection specified for more than four hours per shift."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When a Table 1 control includes an enclosed cab or booth, what must its intake air be filtered through?

options.A: Any filter the equipment maker supplies
options.B: A water spray curtain
options.C: A filter that is 95% efficient in the 0.3-10.0 µm range (e.g., MERV-16 or better)
options.D: An activated carbon filter only

questions.explanation: The enclosed cab or booth must have "intake air that is filtered through a filter that is 95% efficient in the 0.3-10.0 µm range (e.g., MERV-16 or better)".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For tasks done indoors or in enclosed areas while implementing Table 1 controls, what must the employer provide?

options.A: A means of exhaust as needed to minimize the accumulation of visible airborne dust
options.B: Air monitoring every shift
options.C: A HEPA vacuum for each employee
options.D: A second worker to watch for dust

questions.explanation: For tasks performed indoors or in enclosed areas, the employer must "provide a means of exhaust as needed to minimize the accumulation of visible airborne dust".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On Table 1, what respiratory protection is required for a stationary masonry saw used with an integrated water delivery system that continuously feeds water to the blade?

options.A: None, for both four hours or less and more than four hours per shift
options.B: APF 10 for any duration
options.C: APF 10 only for more than four hours per shift
options.D: APF 25 for any duration

questions.explanation: Table 1 row (i) for stationary masonry saws lists the control "Use saw equipped with integrated water delivery system that continuously feeds water to the blade" and "None" in both respiratory protection columns.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On Table 1, a handheld power saw with integrated water delivery is used indoors for four hours or less in a shift. What minimum respiratory protection is listed?

options.A: None
options.B: APF 10
options.C: APF 25
options.D: APF 50

questions.explanation: For handheld power saws (any blade diameter) with water delivery, Table 1 lists "When used indoors or in an enclosed area" as "APF 10" for four hours or less and "APF 10" for more than four hours per shift.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On Table 1, what minimum respiratory protection is listed for handheld grinders for mortar removal (tuckpointing) used more than four hours per shift?

options.A: None
options.B: APF 10
options.C: APF 25
options.D: APF 50

questions.explanation: Table 1 row (xi) lists "Use grinder equipped with commercially available shroud and dust collection system" with APF 10 for four hours or less and "APF 25" for more than four hours per shift.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On Table 1, how must holes be cleaned when using handheld and stand-mounted drills?

options.A: With compressed air
options.B: By dry brushing
options.C: With a wet rag after each shift
options.D: With a HEPA-filtered vacuum

questions.explanation: The Table 1 controls for handheld and stand-mounted drills include "Use a HEPA-filtered vacuum when cleaning holes".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employees' designated representative observes silica air monitoring in an area where protective clothing or equipment is required for a workplace hazard. What must the employer do?

options.A: Keep the observer out of the area
options.B: Charge the observer for the equipment used
options.C: Let the observer enter without equipment if escorted
options.D: Provide the observer with protective clothing and equipment at no cost and ensure the observer uses it

questions.explanation: In that case "the employer shall provide the observer with protective clothing and equipment at no cost and shall ensure that the observer uses such clothing and equipment."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the scheduled monitoring option, the most recent monitoring shows exposures at or above the action level but at or below the PEL. What deadline does the rule set for repeating monitoring?

options.A: Within six months of the most recent monitoring
options.B: Within one year of the most recent monitoring
options.C: Within three months of the most recent monitoring
options.D: Only when the job ends

questions.explanation: Where the most recent monitoring shows exposures "at or above the action level but at or below the PEL, the employer shall repeat such monitoring within six months of the most recent monitoring."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the scheduled monitoring option, the most recent monitoring shows exposures above the PEL. What deadline does the rule set for repeating monitoring?

options.A: Within six months
options.B: Within one year
options.C: Within three months of the most recent monitoring
options.D: Only when the project ends

questions.explanation: Where the most recent monitoring shows exposures "above the PEL, the employer shall repeat such monitoring within three months of the most recent monitoring."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An exposure assessment indicates that employee exposure to respirable crystalline silica is above the PEL. Under 1926.1153(d)(2)(vi)(B), what must the employer describe in the written notification?

options.A: The laboratory's fee for analyzing the samples
options.B: The corrective action being taken to reduce employee exposure to or below the PEL
options.C: The names of employees who declined respirators
options.D: The date of OSHA's next inspection of the site

questions.explanation: "Whenever an exposure assessment indicates that employee exposure is above the PEL, the employer shall describe in the written notification the corrective action being taken to reduce employee exposure to or below the PEL."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When does 1926.1153 allow dry sweeping where it could contribute to employee exposure to respirable crystalline silica?

options.A: Only when wet sweeping, HEPA-filtered vacuuming or other methods that minimize the likelihood of exposure are not feasible
options.B: Whenever employees wear respirators
options.C: At the end of every shift
options.D: Whenever the work is done outdoors

questions.explanation: The employer "shall not allow dry sweeping or dry brushing" where it could contribute to exposure "unless wet sweeping, HEPA-filtered vacuuming or other methods that minimize the likelihood of exposure are not feasible."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.1153(g)(3), to whom must the employer make the written exposure control plan readily available for examination and copying, upon request?

options.A: Only the employer's insurance carrier
options.B: Each employee covered by the section, their designated representatives, the Assistant Secretary and the Director
options.C: Only OSHA compliance officers
options.D: Only the competent person

questions.explanation: "The employer shall make the written exposure control plan readily available for examination and copying, upon request, to each employee covered by this section, their designated representatives, the Assistant Secretary and the Director."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.1153, Respirable crystalline silica (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Periodic medical examinations under 1926.1153(h)(3) include the procedures of the initial examination in paragraph (h)(2), with one exception. Which (h)(2) procedure is left out of the periodic examinations?

options.A: A chest X-ray
options.B: A pulmonary function test
options.C: A physical examination with special emphasis on the respiratory system
options.D: Testing for latent tuberculosis infection

questions.explanation: Periodic examinations "include the procedures described in paragraph (h)(2) of this section (except paragraph (h)(2)(v))", and paragraph (h)(2)(v) is "Testing for latent tuberculosis infection". They are made available "at least every three years, or more frequently if recommended by the PLHCP."

questions.topic: Communication of hazards, training and records
questions.question: Which hazards of respirable crystalline silica must the employer at least address in its hazard communication program?

options.A: Noise, vibration, heat and cold
options.B: Burns, cuts, falls and eye injuries
options.C: Cancer, lung effects, immune system effects and kidney effects
options.D: Fire, explosion, corrosion and reactivity

questions.explanation: The employer must ensure that "at least the following hazards are addressed: Cancer, lung effects, immune system effects, and kidney effects."
